papers.title: Bank loan analysis using customer usage data: A big data approach using Hadoop
papers.evidence: PDF pp. 3–7, dataset, results and conclusion
papers.focus: Historical, descriptive Lending Club loan analysis using Hadoop/HDFS/Hive/HiveQL.
findings: The paper reports debt consolidation as 58.88% of loan purposes (p. 4).
Reported mean interest rates: 11.21% for 36-month loans, 15.32% for 60-month loans, and 12.18% overall (pp. 4, 7).
The paper presents loan-issuance, status and grade-based summaries. It does not report trained-model accuracy, recall, F1 or ROC-AUC for its own analysis.

papers.title: Assessing Fairness and Transparency in Credit Scoring Using Explainable AI
papers.evidence: PDF p. 3, Section III; pp. 5–6, Section IV and Table V
papers.focus: Lending Club classification using Random Forest, LightGBM and XGBoost; SHAP-based interpretation is described.
findings: Table V reports the highest model scores for XGBoost: accuracy 0.8285, recall 0.7425, F1 0.8123 and AUC 0.8988.
LightGBM is close behind in Table V: accuracy 0.8284, recall 0.7412, F1 0.8111 and AUC 0.8981.

The supplied paper describes undersampling and qualitative SHAP feature interpretations. It does not provide numeric home-ownership FPR/recall gaps or a controlled Hive storage/materialization benchmark.

capabilities.ours: 1,000 paired row-bootstrap samples; frozen file fingerprints; equivalent-feature replay and exact metric replay with original row order.
Single-host WSL2/Docker, Hive 4.2.1, HDFS/YARN/Tez; Python model training outside Hive.

cautions: These are side-by-side reported results, not a controlled head-to-head benchmark. We did not reproduce either paper’s full experimental setup.

Cohort, predictor set, target mapping, sampling and split definitions differ or are insufficiently specified. The 2025 paper states undersampling; our test cohort retains its selected natural imbalance (14.13% charged off).
Threshold-dependent accuracy, recall and F1 also depend on decision rules. AUC is threshold-independent; its difference cannot be explained by the 0.15 threshold or imbalance alone.

The 2025 paper’s displayed confusion-matrix totals differ across models: 97,622 for RF/XGBoost and 65,082 for LightGBM (Figures 2–4). Table V is reproduced as author-reported, without silently reconciling those totals or recalculating its metrics.
No claim is made that our model is more accurate than the 2025 models, that our pipeline is 10.44 times faster than either paper, or that our group audit proves fairness.
CatBoost and Adaptive Random Forest were proposed after the original test results were known; their historical holdout comparisons are exploratory, not fresh confirmatory tests.
references.contribution: Our added work is the controlled equivalent-feature Hive pipeline benchmark, explicit preparation/storage measurements, quantitative home-ownership error audit and reproducibility evidence. Our reported predictive scores are lower than the 2025 paper’s scores, and SHAP is not implemented here.
references.dataset_reference: wordsforthewise/Lending Club on Kaggle is the data source, not a third research paper with performance results.
references.comparison_scope: Original models plus CatBoost and Adaptive Random Forest extension; published results were not rerun.

limitations: Extension experiment: the original test results were already known before these models were proposed. This reused historical holdout is not a fresh confirmatory test.
No model tuning or learning uses test outcomes. Thresholds use the original validation-only maximum-F1 grid.
ARF learns only the training partition, ordered by issue month and loan ID; it is frozen for validation/test. These results do not demonstrate live drift adaptation.
Loan outcomes are delayed. The retrospective issue-date split is not a valid prospective label-arrival simulation.
One fixed configuration and seed per new model; no new significance claim, fairness mitigation or new algorithm is established.
Home ownership is a predictor and an audit grouping; protected-group or causal fairness is not established.
